title: ATO raids dentist over early access
full_text:
The ATO has searched a dental practice it alleges was involved in nearly 1200 applications to illegally access superannuation that resulted in the early release of more than $36 million.
The regulator stated that with support from the Australian Federal Police, ATO officers had executed a search warrant at a Melbourne dental practice that was linked to a former health practitioner suspected of supporting individuals to engage in the illegal early access of superannuation by falsely claiming to have compassionate grounds.
“It is alleged the health practitioner supplied fraudulent medical reports to support compassionate release of super applications for dental treatment where applicants were ineligible or the dental work was never provided,” the ATO stated.
“It is further alleged the practitioner supported 1178 compassionate release applications, resulting in the early release of more than $36.4 million from Australian super savings.
“The practitioner is also alleged to have used recruiters to attract individuals into the scheme and facilitate fraudulent applications,” it added, noting investigations were ongoing.
ATO acting deputy commissioner Pennie Snowden said the alleged actions of the health practitioner were not a misunderstanding of the compassionate grounds rules, but indicated a deliberate attempt to take advantage of a feature of the superannuation system meant to help people in genuine need.
“Compassionate release provisions are intended as a last resort to help Australians to access necessary medical treatment not readily available through the public health system,” Snowden added.
“We are increasingly concerned by reports of health practitioners who are exploiting those arrangements to support ineligible access to superannuation.”
The search and comments follow a statement from the ATO and Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) last week in which they highlighted their work in targeting health practitioners and third-party facilitators, including dentists, who encourage individuals to inappropriately access their superannuation to fund cosmetic dental procedures.
Since 1 July 2025, the ATO has undertaken more than 160 reviews and audits involving suspected false or misleading statements in applications and medical reports, and imposed penalties of over $1.5 million.
The regulator is also calling for anyone aware of any practices leading to inappropriate early access of superannuation or health practitioners providing inaccurate medical reports to make a tip-off via its website or report concerns about a practitioner’s conduct or professional performance to AHPRA.
